Heard Ms. Anita Singh, learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. appearing on behalf of the State and perused the material available on record.

No one appears on behalf of opposite party no.
2.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against the order dated 05.01.2022 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST) Act, Firozabad, whereby the learned Judge has rejected the appellant's Bail Application No. 4213 of 2021 arising out of Case Crime No. 03 of 2001, under Sections 376, 394 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)5 of SC/ST Act, Police Station Linepar, District Firozabad.

sentences.text: It is submitted in the affidavit filed in support of this appeal that appellant was enlarged on bail in the year 2001.
He had gone to Gujarat in order to earn his livelihood, therefore, he could not appear before the Trial Court.
He had instructed his counsel to represent him but as no exemption application was filed on his behalf, NBW was issued against him and since then he is in jail.
It is submitted that the appellant shall regularly attend the Court and cooperate in trial.
It is in the last submitted that the appellant is in jail since 13.11.2018 and in case he is released on bail he will not Rinkoo @ Raju vs State Of U.P. Through Its Principal ...

1 misuse the liberty of bail.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant, but could not dispute the aforesaid factum of the case as argued by the learned counsel for the appellant.

Considering the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties, facts and circumstances of the case,
nature of the offence, evidence appearing in the case, the fact that the appellant was earlier on bail,
the fact that the appellant is in jail since 13.11.2018, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
Accordingly, the appeal is hereby allowed.
The impugned order dated 05.01.2022 rejecting the bail application of the appellant is hereby set aside.

Let the appellant Rinkoo alias Raju be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) That the appellant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the appellant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned before the release of the appellant on bail.
It is made clear that in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the appellant.

It is also made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court/J.J.Board shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusion on the basis of evidence led, uninfluenced by any finding or observation whatsoever in this order.
